posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: When the emulsion of a transmission hologram shrinks or expands, the Bragg Angle changes. But could the emulsion still be used as a transmission hologram by changing the reference angle? Or would it now only re-play when using a different wavelength?

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md: It replays using a new angle. A transmission hologram actually reconstructs using multiple wavelengths (the full range really) but you get distortion as you move away from the original wavelength. For most visual work the distortion is negligible unless you're working with people as subjects.

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md:
> **Hans:** When the emulsion of a transmission hologram shrinks or expands, the Bragg Angle changes. But could the emulsion still be used as a transmission hologram by changing the reference angle? Or would it now only re-play when using a different wavelength?

a transmission hologram will act as a lens does ,the replay angle will shift as the wavelenght changes, if the film shrinks ,the bragg planes will lay down causing you to skew your plate further from normal

> **MichaelH:** For most visual work the distortion is negligible

This is very true. I made DCG reflections from Michaels silver tranmissions. His tranmission were made with a red laser and I assume he did not induce shrinkage as he used red for his copying. I shot the H2 in green and never worried about any angles except for putting the plate at the angle that yielded the brightest real image, then putting the DCG plate where I wanted it. 

I personally think the copy came out superb! What do you think?

Now to ellaborate, why not just take your MBDCG reflection hologram and make a proximity copy? All you have to do it get the reflection master to replay in red or white.

Keep us posted on how your DCG tranmission turn out!
